A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ArtiHippo research despite the changed title. Their complete 28-page texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original VDD and 5-Dataset experiments, ablations, CLIP transfer/OOD results, and preliminary class-incremental results.

after.justification: V3 reports original VDD and 5-Dataset experiments, task-to-task comparisons, component ablations, and parameter-growth analyses.

M1.justification: V2 Section 2.2.2 samples an existing expert, then makes a retain/ignore decision before selecting an operation. V3 Section 3.2.2 instead includes an Ignore pseudo-expert in the initial softmax, changing the core sampling probabilities. V3 also introduces ArtiHippo-T2T, which learns each task directly from the ImageNet backbone, and removes v2's class-incremental inference extensions.

E1.justification: VDD and 5-Dataset coverage remains, but v3 removes the CLIP-transfer evaluation on ImageNet-Sketch, ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-A, and ImageNet-R from v2 Appendix D. It also removes ArtiHippo's task-ID-free/class-incremental tests from Appendix J. The new task-to-task comparisons use existing VDD tasks.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated comparisons with SupSup-Proj, EFT, and Lightweight Learner in Table 4, and EWC, L2 regularization, and Experience Replay in Table 7. Removing v2's CLIP-transfer experiment also removes its comparisons with zero-shot CLIP, full fine-tuning, LoRA, and Zero-Init Attention.

E3.justification: Reported ArtiHippo supernet budgets change from 300 to 150 epochs on VDD and from 150 to 50 on 5-Dataset. L2G budgets change from 150/50 to 50/25 epochs respectively, and the task-token learning rate changes from 0.003 to 0.001. V3 adds the fixed-ImageNet task-to-task protocol and parameter-cost measurements in the component comparison. Retained dataset splits are unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 expands the component ablation with Key and parameter-cost comparisons, adds prompted exploration-exploitation curves, and introduces parameter-growth analysis against All New and All Adapt controls in Figure 6. Architecture case studies are revised, while v2's CLIP OOD analysis disappears. The hybrid-adapter ablation is retained unchanged as Table 5 rather than Table 4.

E5.justification: V3 adds uncertainty values for S-Prompts on 5-Dataset, where v2 reported only means; both describe averaging over five task orders. The sampling-budget figure changes its reported aggregation from two task sequences with three seeded runs each to three seeded runs without specifying two sequences. Main VDD reporting remains based on three seeds.

E6.justification: Many results are replaced under changed sampling and training settings. Hierarchical VDD accuracy changes from 80.11±1.17 to 82.60±0.55, while 5-Dataset ArtiHippo accuracy changes from 96.52±0.40 to 94.33±0.45. Reported parameter change switches from a reduction of 0.92M/task to an increase of 0.68M/task. V3 adds comparison and growth results and removes CLIP/class-incremental results. These differences do not establish performance gains under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: V3 introduces the formal score S_ignore(t) = -max_e S_e(t) and revises the sampling distribution to include that pseudo-expert. V2 Appendix J's task-selection definitions, including Equation 11, are removed. The ViT, accuracy, forgetting, L2G, and SPOS equations otherwise remain or are relocated; there is no new theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The central projection-layer, four-operation NAS, zero-forgetting, and prompt-complementarity claims remain. V3 adds adapting existing CNN-based methods to ViTs as an explicit contribution. V2's introduction claims demonstrated potential for class-incremental learning; v3 places that extension entirely in future work and foregrounds the task-incremental scope.

C2.justification: The component interpretation changes substantially: v2 describes FFN as unsuitable and Value as slightly better than Projection, whereas v3 describes FFN as accuracy-competitive but more costly and Projection as better than Value. V3 adds an empirical sublinear-growth interpretation and qualifies the fairness of its additional class-incremental baselines. V2's explicit search-overhead limitation and task-agnostic failure analysis disappear, although task-ID dependence remains stated.

D1.justification: V3 documents how SupSup, EFT, and Lightweight Learner are implemented for ViTs, revises training hyperparameters, and reports an A100 instead of a Quadro RTX 8000 for the main benchmarks. Log instructions change from artihippo/logs to artihippo/artifacts. The detailed CLIP-transfer training recipe, hardware specification, and associated code/configuration instructions are removed.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion and citations for SupSup, EFT, Lightweight Learner, CLR, calibration, and related implementation techniques, while removing references associated with the CLIP/OOD extension, including LoRA and LLaMA-Adapter. Figure 1 clarifies its relationship to parameter-tuning approaches. The main positioning around Learn to Grow, SPOS, and complementary prompting remains.

P1.justification: V3 retitles the paper, substantially rewrites the abstract and introduction, separates Related Work and Our Contributions, and moves identification analysis and metric definitions into Appendix B. It replaces the separate Limitations, Broader Impact, and Conclusions sections with Discussion and Conclusion and substantially reorganizes the appendices.

P2.justification: V3 adds the conceptual comparison Figure 1 and task-to-task Table 4, redraws the sampling and architecture diagrams, expands the sampling figure with prompted curves and a parameter-growth panel, and adds a parameter-cost column to the component table. CLIP and class-incremental tables disappear. Typography, headers, author layout, and figure/table placement are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: V3 better supports its task-incremental contribution through comparisons using the same backbone with SupSup/EFT/Lightweight Learner, documented baseline adaptations, and component-cost and parameter-growth analyses. These provide a limited net improvement in empirical support. Removing explicit search-overhead discussion and task-agnostic failure evidence weakens transparency and limits the gain. Revised accuracy values themselves do not establish improvement because the sampler and training budgets also change.
